رَعِيبٌ Afraid, or frightened, or terrified: (K:) [or filled with fear: or in a state of the utmost fear or terror: (see 1:)] and so ↓ مَرْعُوبٌ , (S, K,) and ↓ مُرَعَّبٌ , and ↓ مُرْتَعِبٌ : (TA:) and ↓ رُعْبُوبٌ signifies [the same; or] weak and cowardly. (S, K.) [Hence,] رَجُلٌ رَعِيبُ العَيْنِ and ↓ مَرْعُوبُهَا and ↓ رُعْبُوبُهَا (tropical:) A cowardly man, who sees nothing without being frightened. (A.) [رَغِيبُ العَيْنِ has a different meaning: see art رغب.] ―
-b2- Also Fat, as an epithet; (K;) dripping with grease: (S, K:) and so ↓ مُرَعْبِبٌ . (K.) And applied to a camel's hump as meaning Full and fat. (S.) ―
-b3- And Short; as also ↓ أَرْعَبُ : pl. [of the former] رُعُبٌ and [of the latter] رُعْبٌ. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
